chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who performed tamattuʿ hajj while not having with him what he could buy a sacrificial offering with; then, after he had fasted three days during the hajj, he became financially able. Should he buy a sacrificial offering and slaughter it, or leave that and fast seven days when he returns to his family?
He عليه السلام said: He should buy a sacrificial offering and slaughter it, and the fasting that he already performed will count as supererogatory for him.

The proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a degree of recommendation and desirability, because whoever obtains the price of the sacrificial offering after having fasted three days has the choice: if he wishes, he may fast the remainder of what is due upon him, and if he wishes, he may slaughter the sacrificial offering; and the sacrificial offering is more virtuous.

key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: the sacrificial offering, considered superior here
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the option between two valid courses
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: supererogatory, not counted as the obligatory substitute
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering required in the context of tamattuʿ hajj

ai.seo_question: If a tamattuʿ pilgrim fasts because he cannot afford the hady and then later becomes able, must he slaughter the hady or complete the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ hajj who could not initially afford the hady and therefore began the substitute fast. If he later becomes able after fasting three days, the report states that he may offer the hady, while the concluding legal note explains that this is to be understood as recommended, and that he is given a choice, though offering the hady is superior.
